scope: Eight corrections after all published reuse questions were compared with chapter I uses; 24 new bands
note: Separated eight misleading published question sets from their chapter I senses. All 236 draft meanings now have contextual question records; no published question or mastery was changed.

items.reviewNote: Published same-form questions were checked against this source use: J’ai eu l’honneur de connaître expresses the privilege of meeting him. All three published same-form questions concern moral reputation or dignity instead. The new answer sequence is the privilege, honneur, honneur; each distractor was checked against its sentence, including grammatical agreement.

Published same-form questions were checked against this source use: De la tête aux pieds measures the body from its literal head. The published three-band questions all teach taking the lead or front of a group. The new answer sequence is head, tête, tête; each distractor was checked against its sentence, including grammatical agreement.

Published same-form questions were checked against this source use: The three chapter I uses compare Earth as a planet with Sirius and Saturn; all published same-form questions teach soil for gardening. Later workwide uses need their own contextual scope. The new answer sequence is Earth, terre, terre; each distractor was checked against its sentence, including grammatical agreement.

Published same-form questions were checked against this source use: Je rapporterai ici marks the following place in the narrative. All three published same-form questions point to a physical place. The new answer sequence is at this point in the account, ici, ici; each distractor was checked against its sentence, including grammatical agreement.

Published same-form questions were checked against this source use: Micromégas is the protagonist’s given appellation. All three selected published questions instead teach honor or reputation attached to a name. The new answer sequence is name, nom, nom; each distractor was checked against its sentence, including grammatical agreement.

Published same-form questions were checked against this source use: Vers les quatre cent cinquante ans estimates an age. The published same-form question bands all teach motion toward a place. The chapter I poetry noun has its own draft. The new answer sequence is around that age, vers, vers; each distractor was checked against its sentence, including grammatical agreement.

Published same-form questions were checked against this source use: Pas géométriques are standardized five-foot units of length, not ordinary individual walking steps. The published noun quiz bands teach taking a step in motion; negative pas stays in separate reuse. The new answer sequence is paces as length units, pas, pas; each distractor was checked against its sentence, including grammatical agreement.

Published same-form questions were checked against this source use: Au sortir de l’enfance means on leaving childhood, a life stage. All three published question bands teach physically going outside a building. The new answer sequence is on leaving childhood, sortir, sortir; each distractor was checked against its sentence, including grammatical agreement.
